answer: In the olive grove, each registered tree is bolted to its own bedrock anchor, and the grove's shared seismograph logs the pulse every tapping sends down that bolt, timestamped. Seasons of real care change each bolt's coupling, so the pulses drift tree by tree; a cloned grove bolts every copy to one poured slab, so all its pulses carry one signature. The surveyor reads drift, not leaves — a slab-farm collapses into a single flat line, while standing work keeps its own rhythm.
